frontier_question: Why did OpenAI release GPT-5 in August 2025, and what did it change about how the company sells its models?

chunks.content: OpenAI released GPT-5 (with GPT-5 mini) on 2025-08-07, available to free users immediately — a deliberate shift to give-away-the-frontier pricing. GPT-5 retired the separate o-series products: o3, o4-mini, o3-mini and o3-pro were folded into GPT-5's internal "reasoning modes"; OpenAI's pitch was "GPT-5 is not a 'reasoning model'; it's a model that thinks" — one model, no model picker. The features: a 5-million-token context window, native image generation built in (no separate image model), deep research integrated, and file upload and web search out of the box. Pricing: free on the free tier; Plus $20/month (unlimited GPT-5); Pro $200/month; API pricing $1.25 / $10 per million tokens for GPT-5 and $0.25 / $2 for GPT-5 mini. GPT-5 scored about 78.6% on SWE-bench Verified, with GPT-5 mini close behind — both at a fraction of the o-series prices. The launch consolidated OpenAI's strategy around one unified model plus aggressive free-tier distribution: the reasoning-vs-non-reasoning split ended, price collapsed, and the competitive battleground moved from benchmark demos to default agency — models that act, not models that answer.

prior_gap_texts: OpenAI released GPT-5 on August 7, 2025 [Source: ev-1], marking a deliberate strategic shift to "give-away-the-frontier" pricing by making the model available immediately to free users [Source: ev-1].

This release fundamentally changed how OpenAI sells its models by consolidating its product lineup into one unified model and eliminating the previous distinction between reasoning and non-reasoning products [Source: ev-1].

Specifically, GPT-5 retired separate o-series products (o3, o4-mini, o3-mini, and o3-pro), folding their capabilities into internal "reasoning modes," thereby removing the need for a model picker [Source: ev-1].
The new sales approach is characterized by aggressive distribution on the free tier and significantly lower API costs compared to previous generations [Source: ev-1].

While Plus remains at $20/month and Pro at $200/month, API pricing dropped to $1.25 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens for GPT-5, with GPT-5 mini priced even lower at $0.25 / $2 per million tokens [Source: ev-1].
This strategy moved the competitive battleground from benchmark demos to "default agency," focusing on models that act rather than just answer [Source: ev-1].
Despite these changes, performance remained strong, with GPT-5 scoring approximately 78.6% on SWE-bench Verified, while achieving these results at a fraction of o-series prices [Source: ev-1].
